summary30s: The 1989 General Elections ended single-party dominance, inaugurating a 25-year era of multi-party coalition governments at the Centre (1989 to 2014).
The Mandal Commission (appointed 1979 by Janata Party, headed by B.P. Mandal) recommended 27% reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs.
In August 1990, Prime Minister V.P. Singh implemented the Mandal recommendations, triggering widespread student protests; upheld by the Supreme Court in the Indira Sawhney case (1992).
Mandal politics catalysed the rise of OBC and Dalit political assertion, notably Kanshi Ram's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP, founded 1984).
National Front (1989-90) was succeeded by United Front (1996-98), National Democratic Alliance (NDA, 1998-2004), and United Progressive Alliance (UPA, 2004-2014).

coreConcepts.title: The 1989 Turning Point & The Emergence of Coalition Politics
coreConcepts.explanation: The 1989 elections marked a decisive watershed in Indian politics: the definitive end of the 'Congress System' and the advent of multi-party coalition governance. Congress won 197 seats but lacked a majority. V.P. Singh formed the 'National Front' government, supported from outside by two ideologically opposed parties: the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Left Front. Since 1989, no single party won a clear majority in the Lok Sabha until 2014. Coalitions became institutionalized: regional parties (DMK, TDP, AIADMK, Trinamool, RJD, JD(U)) became indispensable kingmakers in central governance.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 1
coreConcepts.examTip: 1989 National Front government under V.P. Singh was supported from outside simultaneously by the BJP and the Left Front.

coreConcepts.title: The Mandal Commission and the 27% OBC Reservation
coreConcepts.explanation: Article 340 authorizes the appointment of a commission to investigate backward classes. The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 under Kaka Kalelkar. In 1979, the Janata Party government appointed the Second Backward Classes Commission, headed by Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal (B.P. Mandal). The Commission submitted its report in 1980, estimating OBCs at 52% of the population and recommending 27% reservation in central government jobs and educational institutions. On 7 August 1990, Prime Minister V.P. Singh announced the implementation of the 27% quota. This ignited violent anti-reservation agitations and student self-immolations. In November 1992, the Supreme Court delivered the historic 'Indira Sawhney case' (Mandal judgment), upholding the 27% quota while ruling that total reservations must not exceed 50% and excluding the 'creamy layer' from benefits.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: B.P. Mandal headed the 2nd Backward Classes Commission (1979). Indira Sawhney judgment (1992) upheld 27% OBC quota with 'creamy layer' exclusion.

coreConcepts.title: Political Fallouts: OBC Mobilization and Dalit Assertion (BSP)
coreConcepts.explanation: The Mandal debate permanently reshaped Indian political sociology. Backward classes mobilized politically, transferring their loyalties from Congress to regional and social-justice parties (Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, Janata Dal-United). Concurrently, Dalit mobilization gained massive momentum. Kanshi Ram founded the BAMCEF (Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation) in 1978, the DS-4 (Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti) in 1981, and finally the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in 1984. Under Kanshi Ram and Mayawati, the BSP mobilized Dalits, OBCs, and minorities, capturing power in Uttar Pradesh in 1995.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: Kanshi Ram founded BAMCEF (1978), DS-4 (1981), and the Bahujan Samaj Party (1984).

coreConcepts.title: Chronology of Coalitions: NF, UF, NDA, and UPA
coreConcepts.explanation: Four major coalition experiments unfolded between 1989 and 2014: (1) National Front (1989-1990): V.P. Singh & Chandra Shekhar, supported by BJP & Left; (2) United Front (1996-1998): H.D. Deve Gowda followed by I.K. Gujral, supported from outside by Congress; (3) National Democratic Alliance (NDA, 1998-2004): Led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, bringing together over 20 parties, completing a full 5-year term (1999-2004); (4) United Progressive Alliance (UPA, 2004-2014): Led by Dr. Manmohan Singh and chaired by Sonia Gandhi, ruling for two full terms (UPA-I supported by Left; UPA-II). In 2014 and 2019, Narendra Modi led the BJP to single-party parliamentary majorities (282 and 303 seats), functioning within the NDA coalition.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 9, Section 4
coreConcepts.examTip: Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first Prime Minister to lead a non-Congress coalition government through a full five-year term (1999-2004).

workedExamples.question:
In which landmark verdict did the Supreme Court of India uphold the constitutional validity of 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) while excluding the 'creamy layer'?
(A) Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)
(B) Minerva Mills case (1980)
(C) Indira Sawhney case (1992)
(D) Shah Bano case (1985)
workedExamples.explanation: In the Indira Sawhney vs Union of India case (November 1992), also known as the Mandal case, the Supreme Court declared the 27% OBC reservation valid, while capping total reservations at 50% and introducing the exclusion of the creamy layer.

commonTraps.misconception: Thinking the Mandal Commission recommended 52% reservation for OBCs.
commonTraps.correctConcept: The Commission estimated that OBCs constituted 52% of India's population, but recommended TWENTY-SEVEN PERCENT (27%) reservation to comply with Supreme Court limits on total quotas.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask 'What percentage of reservation was recommended by the Mandal Commission?' and options list 52% and 27%.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing United Front (1996) with National Front (1989).
commonTraps.correctConcept: National Front (1989, V.P. Singh) was supported by BJP and Left; United Front (1996, Deve Gowda/Gujral) was supported by Congress and opposed by BJP.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Both were non-Congress, non-BJP fronts, leading students to invert their external supporters.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: National Front = BJP + Left support; United Front = Congress support.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year did Prime Minister V.P. Singh announce the implementation of the Mandal Commission's recommendation granting 27% reservation to OBCs?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In August 1990, the National Front government under V.P. Singh decided to implement the recommendation of the Mandal Commission.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Second Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1979 by the Janata Party government?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal was the Chairman of the Second Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1979.

practiceQuestions.question: In which historic judgment of 1992 did the Supreme Court uphold the 27% quota for OBCs while excluding the 'creamy layer'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In the famous Indira Sawhney case (November 1992), the Supreme Court upheld the decision of the government.

practiceQuestions.question: Which Prime Minister led the United Front government formed in 1996 with outside support from the Congress party?
practiceQuestions.explanation: H.D. Deve Gowda was chosen as the Prime Minister of the United Front government in June 1996.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the first non-Congress Prime Minister to complete a full five-year term in office?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Atal Bihari Vajpayee completed a full five-year term as Prime Minister from October 1999 to May 2004.

practiceQuestions.question: What was the name of the government employees' federation founded by Kanshi Ram in 1978 that paved the way for the Bahujan Samaj Party?
practiceQuestions.explanation: BAMCEF (Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation) was formed in 1978 by Kanshi Ram.

practiceQuestions.question: The First Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1953 under Article 340 was headed by:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 under the chairmanship of Kaka Kalelkar.

practiceQuestions.question: In 2008, why did the Left Front parties withdraw their crucial outside support from the UPA-I government under Dr. Manmohan Singh?

options.text: Over the enactment of the Right to Information Act
Over the signing of the Indo-US Civil Nuclear Agreement
Over the reservation of seats for women in Parliament

practiceQuestions.question: What percentage of reservation in central government jobs was recommended by the Mandal Commission for the Other Backward Classes?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservations in government jobs and educational institutions for OBCs.

Reason (R): Since no national party could secure an absolute parliamentary majority between 1989 and 2014, regional parties became indispensable coalition partners, shaping union budgets, federal transfers, and national policies.
